name: Sixteen Personality Traits
subtitle: Personality Factor Analysis
instructions: Rate each statement from 1 (Not at all like me) to 5 (Very much like me). Go with your first honest reaction rather than thinking too long.

questions.text: At a dinner with people you don't know well, you find yourself curious about who they are and what their lives are like.
When someone is talking through a problem with you, you find it easy to stay genuinely engaged rather than waiting for them to finish.
You tend to feel most comfortable around people you already know rather than around strangers.
When a group is trying to sort something out, you often find yourself drawing people together rather than staying to one side.
You feel naturally at ease in situations where you have to mix with people you've never met.
Being around others tends to energize you rather than wear you out.
You find it easy to show warmth toward people, even ones you've only recently met.
You tend to keep a certain distance even in friendships, preferring not to get too close too quickly.
People often describe you as warm or easy to be around.
You find it genuinely interesting to learn about how other people think and what shapes their views.
You generally find it easy to work out the rule behind a sequence of numbers, like which number comes next in a pattern.
When faced with a complex problem, you can usually break it down into its parts without too much difficulty.
Abstract puzzles, things with no clear right or wrong, tend to frustrate you more than engage you.
You pick up on logical inconsistencies in an argument fairly quickly.
When someone explains a complex idea, you tend to follow it without needing it repeated.
Working through problems that require step-by-step reasoning tends to come naturally to you.
You find it harder than most people to hold several pieces of information in mind at once.
Spotting the flaw in a line of reasoning is something you tend to do without much effort.
If someone gives you a set of facts, you can usually draw out the logical conclusion fairly quickly.
When things are explained clearly, you grasp them quickly, but dense or abstract material takes you much longer.
When something frustrating happens during the day, you tend to move past it without it affecting the rest of your day much.
Your mood tends to be fairly consistent, not particularly tied to what happens around you.
You can feel off or unsettled without being able to identify what exactly triggered it.
Even when things go wrong, you generally manage to stay composed and functional.
You tend to handle uncertainty and ambiguity without it making you particularly anxious.
You rarely feel overwhelmed, even during particularly demanding stretches.
You can feel unsettled for reasons that are difficult to explain, even when your circumstances are fine.
Small irritations throughout the day can accumulate and affect your overall mood by the evening.
Your emotional baseline tends toward stability rather than ups and downs.
When you are going through a stressful period, it tends to show in your behavior or mood.
In most situations you find yourself in, you tend to naturally take the lead rather than wait for someone else to.
When you disagree with someone in authority, you are fairly comfortable saying so.
You would describe yourself as someone who asserts their opinions rather than keeping them to themselves.
When a decision needs to be made and no one is stepping up, you tend to be the one who moves things forward.
You find it uncomfortable to push back against people who are more experienced or more senior than you.
You tend to hold your ground in disagreements rather than adjusting your view to match the room.
People who know you would describe you as someone who takes charge, not someone who waits to be told what to do.
When something feels unfair, you are more likely to say something than to let it go.
You feel comfortable setting the direction in situations where no clear structure exists.
You would rather follow a path someone else has set up than have to chart your own.
People who know you well would say you are generally upbeat and easy to be around.
You tend to find humor or lightness in situations where others stay serious.
When you are in a group, you are often one of the louder or more animated voices.
You tend to be spontaneous and enjoy doing things on the spur of the moment.
You are generally described as a serious person more than a playful one.
You find it easy to be expressive and enthusiastic, even with people you don't know well.
You prefer to think carefully before you act rather than trusting your impulse in the moment.
When you're with people you're comfortable around, you tend to be the one keeping the energy up.
You approach most situations with a light touch rather than taking them too seriously.
Your mood tends toward the subdued rather than the expressive end of the spectrum.
You tend to follow through on your commitments even when no one would notice if you didn't.
Rules that exist for a clear reason feel worth following, even when they're inconvenient.
You have been known to take shortcuts when the outcome would be the same either way.
Your behavior tends to stay consistent whether or not you know you're being observed.
You hold yourself to a fairly clear personal code, and it doesn't shift much based on context.
When something feels morally unclear to you, you tend to err on the cautious side.
There are certain things you simply won't do regardless of the benefit involved.
You tend to judge a situation by its outcome rather than whether the process was followed correctly.
You feel genuinely uncomfortable when you do something that conflicts with your own standards, even if no one finds out.
Being seen as a responsible and reliable person matters to you.
Situations that put you in the spotlight, speaking in front of a group or being the center of attention, don't particularly unsettle you.
You tend to approach risky or unfamiliar situations with curiosity rather than hesitation.
Before trying something new, you usually think through what could go wrong.
You are generally comfortable in high-pressure or high-stakes situations.
You would describe yourself as someone who finds challenge energizing rather than draining.
Situations that involve competition or being evaluated tend to make you anxious.
You feel at ease meeting people in positions of authority or status.
You are generally more comfortable with the familiar than you are seeking out new or uncertain experiences.
You can usually hold your nerve in difficult situations that would rattle most people.
Taking on a challenge where there is a real possibility of failing is something you find energizing rather than off-putting.
When you make a decision, how things feel tends to carry at least as much weight as what the facts say.
You tend to notice the aesthetic qualities of things, whether a space is well-designed, whether something looks right.
You find that imagination and possibility matter to you in a way that pure practicality sometimes can't satisfy.
You are drawn more toward ideas and what could be than toward systems and what is.
You tend to trust practical evidence over intuition when the two point in different directions.
Art, music, or literature has a genuine effect on your inner state, not just your intellectual appreciation.
You tend to approach things practically and concretely rather than through feeling or imagination.
You are more swayed by how something feels in practice than by what the theory says.
You find yourself drawn to things that are beautiful or moving, not just useful.
Hard facts and evidence feel more reliable to you than instinct or emotional impression.
When something goes wrong in a group you're part of, your first instinct is to work out who dropped the ball.
You tend to assume that people's motives are mostly self-interested unless you have reason to think otherwise.
When someone is very kind to you without an obvious reason, you sometimes find yourself wondering what they want.
You have a fairly clear sense of who in your life is actually on your side and who isn't.
You tend to take what people say at face value rather than reading into it.
You have sometimes felt that people were getting credit for things that were more yours than theirs.
You tend to interpret ambiguous situations charitably rather than assuming the worst.
You are fairly alert to the possibility that people around you might not have your best interests at heart.
When a colleague takes a different approach to yours, your first instinct is competition rather than curiosity.
You generally trust people until they give you a reason not to.
Your mind tends to wander toward ideas and possibilities even when the situation calls for you to stay focused on what's in front of you.
You tend to prefer working through the practical realities of a situation rather than speculating about possibilities.
You find it easy to get absorbed in a thought or idea even when other things are demanding your attention.
You tend to notice when you're drifting from the practical matter at hand and pull yourself back quickly.
When thinking through a situation, you tend to consider the details of what's actually happening more than the broader meaning behind it.
You find yourself drawn to the abstract or conceptual aspects of things, even in practical contexts.
You tend to be more comfortable working with concrete facts and real situations than with speculation or theory.
Your mind tends toward breadth and possibility rather than depth and precision in any one area.
You find you function better when focused on real, immediate tasks rather than open-ended possibilities.
Being absorbed in your own thoughts is a fairly familiar state for you, even when you're around other people.
You tend to be fairly discreet about your own affairs, not sharing more than is necessary even with people you trust.
In social situations, you tend to observe the dynamics of what's happening rather than simply participating in them.
You find it fairly easy to read between the lines of what people say, noticing what they're not saying as much as what they are.
You can usually tell when someone is trying to manage an impression rather than being straightforwardly themselves.
You tend to say what you mean fairly directly rather than shaping what you say to what others want to hear.
You find it natural to adjust how you present yourself depending on who you're talking to.
You are generally more open and transparent with people than you are guarded or reserved.
You tend to keep your own counsel, sharing your real views selectively rather than broadly.
You are fairly attentive to how you come across in any given situation.
You find it easy to take a step back in a conversation and notice the social dynamics playing out.
You tend to worry about things more than most people around you seem to.
When something is unresolved, you can find it difficult to fully switch off and stop thinking about it.
You handle uncertainty well and don't particularly need things to be resolved before you can feel settled.
There is usually something sitting in the back of your mind that you feel mildly concerned about.
Your mind tends to run through possible problems or complications even when things are going fine.
You feel settled and at ease most of the time, without much of a background sense of unease.
When you're waiting to hear about something important, it tends to occupy your thinking more than it probably should.
You tend to imagine worst-case scenarios more often than you'd prefer.
Things that go wrong rarely stay with you for long.
The idea that something might be going wrong somewhere in your life tends to sit uneasily with you until it's resolved.
You find yourself questioning established ways of doing things when there might be a better approach.
You are generally skeptical of things done a certain way simply because they've always been done that way.
You tend to be more comfortable with convention and proven approaches than with experimenting or changing things.
You find it interesting to debate established ideas rather than accepting them.
You are more likely to follow a tried-and-tested method than to try something new when the outcome matters.
You tend to seek out new information that might change how you understand something.
Being intellectually challenged and having your assumptions tested feels stimulating rather than threatening.
You tend to think that things work well enough as they are rather than needing to be questioned or reimagined.
When you hear a new idea that contradicts what you already think, your first instinct is usually curiosity rather than resistance.
You find comfort in clear, established ways of doing things rather than experimenting with alternatives.
You feel more comfortable making decisions on your own than through a group process.
Given the choice between reaching a decision through discussion or working it through alone, you tend to prefer working it through alone.
You find it natural to check in with others before committing to a course of action.
When you need to think something through, you tend to do it better in your own head than out loud.
You trust your own judgment fairly strongly and don't feel much need to seek outside input before deciding.
You find it easier to act once you have consulted others rather than going on your own instinct alone.
When something important needs to be worked out, your preference is to think it through privately rather than in discussion.
You often find that talking things through with others muddies your thinking rather than clarifying it.
You find the process of group decision-making slow and frustrating compared to just working it out yourself.
You find that getting input from people you trust helps you reach better decisions than going it alone.
You tend to have a clear internal standard for how things should be done, and you hold yourself to it.
When you set yourself a goal, you follow through on it systematically rather than leaving it to chance.
You find it easier to work in a structured, organized way than in a looser, more flexible one.
You can be fairly exacting about how things are done, not just whether they get done.
You tend to finish what you start rather than moving on before something is fully complete.
Doing something in a disorganized or haphazard way tends to bother you even if the outcome is fine.
You tend to approach your responsibilities in a fairly disciplined, methodical way.
You hold a fairly high standard for your own work and tend to notice when it falls short.
When something is worth doing, you tend to want to do it properly rather than adequately.
You tend to feel restless or dissatisfied if things around you are in disorder or not done to a good standard.
There is usually a background level of tension or restlessness running through your days even when nothing particular is wrong.
You tend to feel tense or keyed-up more often than you feel fully relaxed.
You feel genuinely at ease in your body and mind most of the time.
Your energy levels tend to feel slightly depleted or strained rather than full and steady.
You find it hard to truly switch off, even in situations that are meant to be restful.
Even when life is going reasonably well, there is often a low-level feeling of not quite being able to relax.
You tend to feel comfortable and settled in your own skin most of the time.
There tends to be a slight undercurrent of anxiety in your day-to-day experience.
You can feel wound up or on edge without a clear external cause.
Most of the time you feel relatively calm and free of unnecessary internal pressure.
You tend to present yourself honestly rather than trying to manage what people think of you.
There are things about yourself that you would prefer not to examine too closely.
You tend to answer questions about yourself accurately even when the honest answer is unflattering.
